name: Canberra Times cryptic crossword, Saturday 10 June 1972

clue.text: Military bands in place by river

blocks.note: to put something is to place it
the Tees is a river in north-east England

explanation.surface: A regimental band is stationed beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' just sets the river next to the verb; 'Military bands' looks like musicians but means strips of cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Puttees are long cloth strips wound round a soldier's lower legs, part of old army uniform.

clue.text: Journalists have raised food in Bratislava, according to Germans

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word turns it upside down, so it reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: the press is journalists collectively
grub is slang for food

explanation.surface: Reporters in the Slovak capital have been served their meal.
explanation.walkthrough: Pressburg was the German (and old Austrian) name for the city now called Bratislava.
explanation.definitionFit: Speakers of German historically called the Slovak capital by this older city name.

clue.text: Child makes notes?

definitions.note: plural, while the answer is one group of notes

blocks.note: first meaning: one of three children born at one birth
second meaning: in music, three notes played in the time of two

explanation.surface: A youngster writes things down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notes' suggests jotting, but it is musical notes grouped in threes.
explanation.definitionFit: A multiple birth of three produces these siblings, and music uses the same word for a three-note grouping.

clue.text: Have it in mind to amuse

blocks.note: first meaning: to consider or harbour an idea
second meaning: to keep guests or an audience happy

explanation.surface: Someone intends to make others laugh.
explanation.definitionFit: One may consider or harbour a thought, and also delight guests or an audience, with this same verb.

clue.text: Urgent message about pithead concessions

indicators.note: the head of a word is its front, so only its opening letter is kept
about means surrounding, so the distress call wraps round the other piece

blocks.note: SOS is the international distress signal
the opening letter of the word pit, its head

explanation.surface: An urgent telegram arrives about concessions made at the colliery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pithead' reads as one mining word, but it splits into the word pit and its head.
explanation.definitionFit: Sops are small appeasing offers or bribes made to placate someone, i.e. concessions.

clue.text: A meal-lime communication lion

blocks.note: a mess is a communal meal, especially in the forces
a misprint for time, which an age is: a long period
a stray misprinted word with no part in the wordplay

explanation.surface: A note passed at mealtime.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue as printed is garbled: it should read 'A meal-time communication', with the stray word lion an extra misprint.
explanation.definitionFit: A message is any piece of information sent from one person to another.

clue.text: Played in opera for a spell?

definitions.text: Played in opera for a spell?

blocks.clueFragment: Played in opera for a spell?
blocks.note: surface reading: something performed in an opera house for a while
setter's reading: an instrument played in an opera to cast enchantments, which names a Mozart opera

explanation.walkthrough: 'for a spell' sounds like 'for a time', but it means for working magic.
explanation.definitionFit: Mozart's opera takes its title from an enchanted wind instrument whose music protects the hero.

clue.text: Old engine-driver

blocks.note: surface reading: a retired railwayman who drove locomotives
setter's reading: the power that drove old engines

explanation.walkthrough: 'engine-driver' looks like a person; it is the force that drove locomotives before diesel.
explanation.definitionFit: Vapour from boiling water powered the locomotives and machines of the industrial age.

clue.text: Man of figures with a dour disposition? That's about it

indicators.note: a disposition is an arrangement, so the letters are set out in a new order
about means around, so the rearranged letters surround the last word

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
taken as written

explanation.surface: An accountant is known for his gloomy temperament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposition' reads as temperament, matching the dour accountant stereotype, but it signals rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: An auditor examines a company's accounts, so he is a professional who works with numbers.

clue.text: Tree was planted first?

definitions.note: a verb phrase, while the answer is an adjective meaning born earlier

blocks.note: first meaning: a shrub or small tree bearing dark berries
second meaning: older, as if put in the ground earlier

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'planted' is used playfully for being born.
explanation.definitionFit: The elder is a common hedgerow shrub, and an elder sibling is the older one, arriving earlier.

clue.text: Poet gets priest to return

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the short word is read backwards

blocks.note: Eli is the priest who raised Samuel in the Old Testament
taken as written

explanation.surface: A poet persuades a clergyman to come back.
explanation.walkthrough: ELI is a crossword favourite for priest.
explanation.definitionFit: T. S. Eliot wrote The Waste Land and is one of the twentieth century's major poets.

clue.text: Freakishly obstinate?

blocks.note: surface reading: unusually stubborn
setter's reading: a freak with the head of a farmyard animal

explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, the word describes a monster with a swine's head, which would indeed be freakish.
explanation.definitionFit: The word ordinarily means stupidly stubborn, refusing to change one's view.

clue.text: Pay old journalist by the line

blocks.clueFragment: Pay old journalist by the line
blocks.note: surface reading: an instruction to remunerate a hack per line of copy
setter's reading: regular fixed wages, the opposite of being paid by the line

explanation.surface: An editor tells the accounts office how to settle a veteran reporter's fees.
explanation.walkthrough: Old freelance reporters were 'penny-a-liners', paid per line; a staff journalist got fixed regular pay instead.
explanation.definitionFit: A salary is a fixed regular payment for employment, usually monthly.

clue.text: Mark appears around one with German sword

indicators.note: showing up around something means enclosing it, so the mark wraps the other pieces

blocks.note: a scar is a mark left by a wound
Roman numeral one
mit is German for with

explanation.surface: A scar shows where a German swordsman struck.
explanation.definitionFit: A scimitar is a curved single-edged blade of Middle Eastern origin.

clue.text: Recommending some publicity career

blocks.note: an ad, a piece of advertising, is some publicity
a vocation is a calling or career

explanation.surface: A careers adviser suggests a job in public relations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recommending' is a verb form standing for a noun meaning the act of recommending.
explanation.definitionFit: Advocation is the act of arguing for or supporting a cause, i.e. urging it on others.

clue.text: Extreme view of some youthful traveller

indicators.note: only some of the following words is in view, so the answer sits inside them

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A young backpacker holds radical opinions.
explanation.definitionFit: Ultra as an adjective means going beyond the usual, as in ultra-conservative positions.

clue.text: Saved, having been given transplant, perhaps?

definitions.note: a phrase, read as de-livered: supplied with a liver

blocks.note: first meaning: rescued, set free
second meaning, split as de- plus livered: provided with a new liver

explanation.walkthrough: The 'perhaps?' warns that the second meaning is a playful split of the word around the organ.
explanation.definitionFit: To be delivered from danger is to be rescued, and a liver transplant patient is jokingly 'livered'.

clue.text: Game for the majority once

definitions.note: a phrase for an age, read as the French words for twenty-one

blocks.note: first meaning: the card game also called pontoon or blackjack
second meaning: French for twenty-one, which used to be the age of majority

explanation.walkthrough: Until 1969-70 in Britain and Australia one came of age, reaching one's majority, at twenty-one; the voting age then dropped to eighteen.
explanation.definitionFit: The card game in which players aim for a total of twenty-one takes its name from the French number.

clue.text: Calamities upset rates in a Norfolk town

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over and jumbled, so the letters are rearranged
in places the jumbled letters inside the name of the town

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
Diss is a market town in Norfolk, an English county

explanation.surface: A rise in local property taxes causes disasters in a small English town.
explanation.walkthrough: Rates were the local property tax in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Calamities and disasters are both sudden events causing great damage or misfortune.

clue.text: Running short of drink about four — painful thing

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the drink wraps round the number

blocks.note: gin is a spirit
Roman numeral four
gout is a painful inflammation of the joints

explanation.surface: Someone's supply of liquor is running low around four o'clock, which is a pain.
explanation.definitionFit: Supplies that are giving out are becoming exhausted, failing or nearly used up.

clue.text: Part of speech made by girl in the plant

blocks.note: a verb is one of the grammatical parts of speech
Ena is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl gives a speech among the greenery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part of speech' seems to mean an extract from a talk; it is the grammatical term.
explanation.definitionFit: Verbena is a garden flowering herb, also called vervain.

clue.text: King in glasses?

definitions.note: a phrase, standing for a drink served in glasses

blocks.note: first meaning: the title of the Emperor of Ethiopia
second meaning: a hot spiced wine drink served in glasses

explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a monarch wearing spectacles; the glasses are drinking glasses.
explanation.definitionFit: Negus was the Ethiopian royal title, and also an eighteenth-century hot mulled port or sherry drink.

clue.text: Relevant to the European quarter

blocks.note: a German is a European
east is a quarter, one of the four compass points

explanation.surface: Something concerning the European district of a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relevant to' includes 'to', because the answer is used in the phrase germane to.
explanation.definitionFit: Germane means pertinent or closely connected with the matter being discussed.

clue.text: Weapon for a quiet craftsman

blocks.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for soft
an artisan is a skilled manual worker

explanation.surface: A tool or arm suitable for a silent workman.
explanation.walkthrough: A partisan here is not a supporter but a long-handled spear.
explanation.definitionFit: A partisan is a medieval pole arm, a spear with a broad blade and side projections.

clue.text: She has passed in poetry

blocks.note: surface reading: a woman who has died, mourned in verse
setter's reading: the heroine of Robert Browning's verse drama whose title says she passes

explanation.walkthrough: 'has passed' suggests death, but it points at the title of Browning's dramatic poem, Pippa Passes.
explanation.definitionFit: Pippa is the silk-mill girl in Browning's poem whose songs touch people as she walks by.

clue.text: One Irish house of parliament is upset by a war story

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the word reads from the bottom up

blocks.note: Roman numeral one
the Dáil is the lower house of the Irish parliament

explanation.surface: An Irish chamber of deputies is unsettled by a tale of conflict.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's epic poem tells of the Trojan War and the wrath of Achilles.

clue.text: Our first air transport, they told us

definitions.text: Our first air transport, they told us

blocks.note: surface reading: the earliest aircraft we ever flew in
setter's reading: the birds that, children are told, bring babies

explanation.walkthrough: The nursery tale says a baby arrives carried by a large bird, so it was our first flight.
explanation.definitionFit: Storks are tall wading birds which folklore says deliver newborn babies to their parents.

clue.text: Part of Kaspar's grand child's steering apparatus

indicators.note: only a part of the named person is used, so letters at each end are dropped

blocks.note: Kaspar's granddaughter in Southey's poem After Blenheim is little Wilhelmine

explanation.surface: A boy's grandfather's ship has a steering wheel.
explanation.walkthrough: In Southey's poem After Blenheim, old Kaspar talks with his grandchildren Peterkin and little Wilhelmine; the answer sits inside her name.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's helm is the tiller or wheel used to steer it.

clue.text: Big drop in cost including re-hash of epic

indicators.note: rehashing something reworks old material, so these letters are rearranged
including means taking in, so the cost wraps round the rearranged letters

blocks.note: price is what something costs
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A remade blockbuster film suffers a steep fall in box-office takings.
explanation.definitionFit: A precipice is a sheer cliff face, a very steep fall.

clue.text: Craft returns from eastern river

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the pieces are read backwards

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for eastern
the Dart is a river in Devon, England

explanation.surface: A boat comes back from a river in the east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft' looks like a boat; it means a skilled occupation.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade is a skilled handicraft or occupation, such as carpentry.

clue.text: Juan in Hell?

blocks.note: surface reading: the scene from Shaw's Man and Superman where the legendary seducer is damned
setter's reading: the famous Don cast out and banned, read as a ban on a Don

explanation.walkthrough: Don Juan, the legendary libertine, ends up in Hell; split the answer and you get a Don under a ban, while the whole word suits his wild life.
explanation.definitionFit: Abandon means unrestrained freedom of behaviour, and to forsake someone utterly, as Juan is forsaken.

clue.text: Ways in which queen enters woman's address

indicators.note: to enter is to go inside, so the queen sits within the form of address

blocks.note: Queen Anne reigned 1702-14
Mrs is the title used to address a married woman

explanation.surface: A royal visitor walks into a lady's home, minding etiquette.
explanation.definitionFit: Manners are someone's habitual ways of behaving, especially polite social conduct.
